name: Title Tracks
label: Dischord
lede: John Davis spent seven years drumming in Q and Not U, then picked up a guitar, took the vocals and wrote record-collector power pop, some of it mixed in mono.

eras.title: Out from behind the drums
eras.text: After seven years on drums in Q and Not U, John Davis went looking for something poppier. He got there first as half of Georgie James, then alone as Title Tracks, singing and playing guitar.

years.h: Q and Not U finish their tour, then play out at the Black Cat
years.p: The band works through its remaining tour commitments, then plays a short farewell stand at the Black Cat in Washington. John Davis had drummed in it for seven years.

years.cap: Davis on guitar with Georgie James, Mercury Lounge, New York, January 13, 2007
years.h: John Davis and Laura Burhenn start Georgie James over old pop records
years.p: Their common ground is pop from the 1950s to the '70s. As [[Georgie James|c4cfd21d-fd5e-45ae-88f2-413f9e15d944]], with singer and pianist [[Laura Burhenn|50174deb-4b25-41f5-9205-ae7b8b2f2118]], they sign to Saddle Creek and release Places in September 2007.

years.cap: Davis on guitar with Georgie James, Mercury Lounge, New York, January 13, 2007
yt: Georgie James at the Ottobar, Baltimore, March 19, 2008
years.h: Georgie James split, and John Davis starts Title Tracks
years.p: Davis had been writing solo songs since early 2008, while still in the duo. [[Laura Burhenn|50174deb-4b25-41f5-9205-ae7b8b2f2118]] goes on to [[The Mynabirds|daa0c966-31a1-4754-b293-67ffe5b4ac18]].
years.xp:
Georgie James signed to Saddle Creek in spring 2007, after a first single on Burhenn's own Laboratory Records, and Places followed that September.

The split was announced on August 4, 2008, both saying they hoped to focus on solo projects. A full Georgie James set from the Ottobar in Baltimore on March 19 of that year is on video.

eras.title: Pop built from a record collector's shelf
eras.text: Dischord put out the first Title Tracks single; the albums went to Ernest Jenning Record Co. Dischord's bio credits John Davis with an almost scientific approach to songwriting, built on years of crate-digging, radio DJ shifts and touring the world.

years.cap: Every Little Bit Hurts / Found Out, Dischord No. 163
years.src: Dischord: Every Little Bit Hurts · Dischord: Title Tracks
years.h: Title Tracks' only Dischord record costs seven dollars
years.p: Every Little Bit Hurts backed with Found Out, recorded with [[Chad Clark|f3f09e99-e31c-4aa2-99e4-0b4e59e72f87]] of [[Beauty Pill|976b28a1-dd68-4c43-ba08-ba15b58963b2]], is Dischord No. 163. Live, John Davis is joined by [[Michael Cotterman|c675284d-bfe6-4df0-89fc-0aca7a5372d5]] (bass), [[Andrew Black|dd041cd4-de4e-4b0b-8892-ae31cc97498e]] (drums) and Meredith Munoz (keys, guitar, vocals).
years.xp: The single was recorded at Silver Sonya. The label kept carrying the band's later records in its store, and Dischord's own pages still list all four releases.

years.src: Dischord: It Was Easy · Wikipedia: Title Tracks
years.h: John Davis plays most of It Was Easy himself
years.p: The Ernest Jenning debut re-records both songs from the Dischord single. Guests include saxophonist Kriston Capps and [[Camera Obscura|94219793-a46b-4c39-9397-e05ad633f32d]] singer [[Tracyanne Campbell|4b10d405-48cb-4bf3-b7d0-98b509428f41]].
years.xp:
Dischord's store copy calls Title Tracks the solo band of Davis, formerly of Q and Not U, and flags that Every Little Bit Hurts and Found Out appear here in different versions.

The live band that toured the record from February through May was Michael Cotterman, Andrew Black and Meredith Munoz.

yt: Piles of Paper, live on KEXP at SXSW, March 17, 2010
years.h: Title Tracks spend four months touring North America
years.p: The It Was Easy tour runs from February through May 2010. On March 17, KEXP records the band at SXSW in Austin.

yt: Turn Your Face, from In Blank
years.h: Ten originals and one Flamin' Groovies cover
years.p: In Blank, Title Tracks' second album, comes out on Ernest Jenning and Windian. The phrase is from Dischord's store copy; the cover is I Can't Hide by The Flamin' Groovies.

eras.title: One more long dream
eras.text: Title Tracks return after five years as a trio with Long Dream. It is the last record; the band has been inactive since 2017.

years.cap: Davis at the Rock & Roll Hotel, Washington, October 7, 2016
yt: Low Cool, live for WAMU's Bandwidth.fm, November 2016
years.h: A trio makes Long Dream, with Elmer Sharp on drums
years.p: Title Tracks' third album, on Ernest Jenning, is John Davis, bassist [[Michael Cotterman|c675284d-bfe6-4df0-89fc-0aca7a5372d5]] and drummer Elmer Sharp, the last in a line of drummers that also included [[Mike Sneeringer|50bd1658-4cfa-4e9c-8c33-778d4b6452d6]].

years.cap: Title Tracks at the Rock & Roll Hotel, Washington, October 7, 2016
years.h: After Long Dream, the records and the shows stop
years.p: Dischord lists Title Tracks' active years as 2008–2017, and the band has been inactive since.
